response: Yes, certain polymorphisms of the angiotensin-converting enzyme-1 (ACE-1) gene have been associated with an increased risk of developing chronic kidney disease (CKD) among hypertensive patients. The insertion/deletion (I/D) polymorphism, in particular, has been studied extensively, with the DD genotype being linked to higher ACE activity, increased blood pressure, and a greater risk of CKD progression in hypertensive individuals. However, it's essential to note that the relationship between ACE-1 gene polymorphism and CKD is complex and influenced by multiple factors, including environmental and genetic interactions.
